summary: Yahweh takes a tender shoot from a cedar and plants it on a mountain, where it branches and bears fruit. Psalm 1 pictures the person who delights in Yahweh’s instruction as a tree planted beside streams, with water enough to bear fruit in season.

stems.gloss: set a plant where it will grow

senses.gloss: plant a tree, vine or cutting
senses.definition: Set a living plant in a place where it can take root. Ezekiel describes taking a tender shoot from one tree and planting it elsewhere.

senses.gloss: be planted, of a person pictured as a tree
senses.definition: The passive participle pictures people established where they can flourish. Beside the stream the tree keeps its leaves through heat and drought, and in Yahweh’s courts the righteous still bear fruit in old age.
Psalm 128 pictures sons gathered around the family table as young olive shoots. This is the noun’s only occurrence.

evidence.note: A man plants for his son as his ancestors planted for him.

note: Ezekiel 17 explicitly describes a transplant. Psalm 128 does not say whether the olive shoots have been moved. The Akkadian noun supports the sense of the Hebrew noun. The proposed borrowing of the verb from Akkadian satālu still needs independent evidence.
